subject: research/selfrep-materials
professional: a materials-flow / industrial-ecology researcher who has published on distributed recycling and 3D-printer life-cycle energy (the Pearce-group Recyclebot and Kreiger LCA kind), who would check first where the part masses and the specific energies come from

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py`; regenerated results.txt is byte-identical to the committed one (git status clean). Recomputed independently with a throwaway script that reads only the BOM and applies the README formulas by hand: 44 printed parts x 25 g = 1.100 kg, F = 1.2222 kg, virgin filament with recycling 1.1244 kg (README 1.12); printer-alone vitamins 5.260 kg (README 5.26); full-shop total with casting 6.4546 kg (README 6.46) and aluminium remelt energy 0.081 kWh (README 0.08); end-of-life case eol=1, phi=0.3 gives 0.8556 and phi=0.8 gives 0.2444 (README 0.86 and 0.24); Al melt energy at 100% efficiency 0.2703 kWh/kg (file 0.270). All arithmetic reproduces, so the model does what it says. Capped at 2 because every driving input is an invented placeholder (part masses, yields, specific energies), so the outputs are not right about any real printer: the 1.1 kg of printed plastic is 44 parts at a flat assumed 25 g, and the 5.26 kg vitamin mass includes box-size fastener lines (100 M8 nuts, 100 washers) that one printer does not use (stated in the bom.py docstring, not carried into this README). The Monte Carlo quantiles were not re-derived independently (only re-run).
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim: the three-shop table (matches results.txt), vitamin share 73-77% over draws (0.728-0.770 in results.txt), 'virgin filament largest in all 2000 draws' (2000/2000), cut of 1-6% (0.010-0.061), eol scenarios, energy split, experiments/figure.png exists, Limitations and Owner steps present. All worked end to end. Not done and said so: recycling machines have no BOM, the melt constants are unchecked against a handbook, no time dynamics. No TODO stubs or dead links found.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 10 tests OK. Seeded three mutants in balance.py, reverting each with git checkout: (1) recycled cap `phi*F` -> `phi*P`: caught (1 failure); (2) remelt `off*(1-m_loss)` -> `off*(1+m_loss)`: caught (1 failure); (3) aluminium melt energy line replaced by 0.0: NOT caught, all 10 pass. No test touches any energy figure except the standalone melt formula, and none checks results.txt, the Monte Carlo, or the parameter-validity range (s=1 would divide by zero). Mass-conservation and closed-form tests are good, but one of three core mutants survives and the headline energy numbers are unguarded.
evidence.craft: Read balance.py, tests/test_balance.py, experiments/run.py, pyproject.toml, and the bom.py/closure.py it imports. Clear docstring with the model equations, frozen dataclass of parameters, small functions, mass-conservation accounting built into the return dict. Defects: sys.path hack to a sibling tree while pyproject declares `dependencies = []` so the package cannot be installed alone; SHOPS re-exported with noqa; run.py is one long module-level script (Monte Carlo inline, not importable or testable); no input validation on s, y_metal, furnace_eff; the energy for machining is charged on product mass not removed mass, though the docstring says 'per kg removed or cut'; sampling stat `q` uses floor index not interpolation (harmless).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'every process parameter is an assumption', 'Nothing here is measured', 'Stylised', the melt constants 'typed from memory and not checked' (I checked: cp 0.90 kJ/kgK is the 25 C value, 397 kJ/kg latent is right, the mean cp 20-660 C is nearer 1.0 so sensible heat is ~10% low and the 100%-efficiency figure should be ~0.29 not 0.27 kWh/kg, within the test's delta; the disclosure covers it), 'builds on selfrep-closure' (true, it imports it), 'no external model is reproduced', every table number (backed by results.txt, reproduced above). The limits are stated and honest, with no overstated finding; the conclusion is explicitly 'structure not magnitudes'. Minor: 'Recycling the shop's own scrap barely helps' is partly an artefact of the assumed s=0.10 scrap, but the sweep range (0.02-0.30) is in the file.
evidence.fitness: For a researcher: could they build on it? The structure (feedstock, yield, scrap, cap) is generic and the code is easy to extend, but the result 'vitamins dominate, own-scrap recycling is small' follows almost by construction from the assumed BOM masses and a 10% scrap rate, so it is not a finding someone could cite. Not a programme step toward a named venue (research/PROGRAMMES.md bar is PhD level and publishable). Nearest prior work, none of which it uses: Jones et al., Robotica 29(1) 2011 (RepRap); Baechler, Devor, Pearce, Rapid Prototyping Journal 2013 (Recyclebot, distributed recycling of waste polymer into RepRap filament, with measured extrusion energy); Kreiger and Pearce, ACS Sustainable Chem. Eng. 2013 (life-cycle energy of distributed printing, measured printer power); Freitas and Merkle, Kinematic Self-Replicating Machines 2004 (materials closure of self-replicators). Measured recycled-filament data and printer energy exist in that literature and would replace phi, e_print, e_shred, e_extrude, which the repo's own rule ('run the numbers; don't stylise them', research/CLAUDE.md) says to source when findable. Novelty over prior work is not shown.
evidence.domain: A researcher in distributed recycling would first ask where the masses and kWh/kg come from; the answer is 'round numbers I chose'. Departures: (a) part masses are flat assumed placeholders, with a one-hour weigh-in of a real Mendel parts list as the cheap fix; (b) fastener quantities are box sizes, inflating the vitamin share headline; (c) remelted aluminium offcuts are credited against imported *sheet*, but a casting shop makes ingot/castings not rolled sheet, so the 0.06 kg saving is not like-for-like; (d) recycled-plastic degradation is one scalar cap with no property data, though measured tensile loss per recycle pass is published; (e) the recycling machines (shredder, extruder, furnace) are absent from the BOM, which is the central question for a self-replicating shop; (f) no uncertainty on the BOM itself, only on process parameters. Method structure is sound and the mass-balance bookkeeping is correct, but it would not be signed off as an estimate of anything real.

defects.what: Headline magnitudes (75-82% vitamin share, 1.1 kg printed plastic, 3% recycling cut) rest on invented inputs although the repo's research rule requires sourcing findable parameters; printed plastic is 44 parts at a flat 25 g, and vitamin mass includes box-size fastener lines (100 nuts, 100 washers) one printer does not use. The README discloses 'stylised' but not the box-size inflation.
Remelted aluminium offcuts are credited against imported aluminium sheet, which a shop with casting cannot produce; the 0.06 kg saving and the 6.62 to 6.46 casting row are not like-for-like.
Mutation survives: replacing the aluminium melt energy by 0 leaves all 10 tests passing; no test covers any energy total or results.txt / Monte Carlo output.
The recycling machines (shredder, extruder, furnace) are not in the copy's bill of materials, so the closure question the project is about is left open.
Aluminium sensible heat uses a constant cp of 0.90 kJ/kgK (25 C value); the 20-660 C mean is ~1.0, so melt energy is ~7% low. README says unchecked; the fix is a two-line constant plus the test.

Package cannot be installed alone (sys.path hack to sibling selfrep-closure, pyproject dependencies empty); machining energy charged on product mass though docstring says per kg removed; no validation of s, y_metal, furnace_eff.

verdict: A small, clean, honest mass-and-energy bookkeeping model: tests pass (10), results.txt regenerates byte-identically, and five headline numbers recompute exactly from the formulas by an independent script, with accurate disclosure that all inputs are assumed. It does not meet the bar: correctness is capped at 2 because the outputs are only as good as invented placeholder masses and energies (including box-size fastener counts inflating the vitamin share), verification is 2 because a seeded mutation zeroing the melt energy survived all tests, and as research it is a stylised exercise with no sourced data and no result new relative to RepRap, Recyclebot and printer-LCA literature, which the repo's own 'run the numbers' rule says to use. Finished, yes (completeness 3); expert-grade, no. A cheap upgrade path: source printer and extruder energy and recycled-filament property loss from the Pearce-group papers, weigh real parts, add the recycling machines to the BOM.
